heckles.message: Your mill and open bays on the floor, shop sound with hum, chatter and the odd squeal, bigger order board
heckles.heckle:
274 lines added and 83 deleted in a single html file, and the headline feature is a shop that squeals. Congratulations, you built a tycoon game with the ambiance of a dentist drill. mill-ionaire-v2.html is now a monolith where CSS, markup, game logic, and audio synthesis all live in one file, and every commit makes the diff harder to read than a congressional spending bill. The new soundBtn is a 32 pixel square next to the 32 pixel info button, two tiny targets jammed together on a phone header, which is exactly how people fat-finger the wrong one. The test click coordinates for the floor mill got nudged from 0.1 to 0.5 and 0.06, so your tests are tied to pixel positions and will break on the next layout tweak.

Fix it: Split mill-ionaire-v2.html into separate css, js and audio files. Give soundBtn and infoBtn at least 44 pixel hit areas and more gap. Click floor mills in the test by selector, not by fraction of the canvas.

heckles.message: Alphabet run and millwright buttons move onto the mill, room for the start marker
heckles.heckle:
You moved two buttons from the menu onto the mill screen and added a mystery PNG named mb.png at the repo root with no explanation. Is it a screenshot, an asset, or a leftover from whatever you were fumbling with at midnight? Binary junk in the root of a repo is how a tidy project turns into a garage sale. In mill-ionaire-v2.html the new .beacon-room rule uses margin-top with important, which is the CSS equivalent of shouting louder when nobody listens. And you whittled the test items list in mill-ionaire-v2-test.js by removing fixBtn from the menu loop, so the millwright is only covered by one click and no assertion about what it fixed.

Fix it: Delete mb.png from the root or move it into an assets folder and say what it is. Remove the important flag on .beacon-room in mill-ionaire-v2.html and fix the specificity properly. Assert in mill-ionaire-v2-test.js that the millwright button actually repairs the machine.

heckles.message: Smaller blue i button, i button and how to play share one sheet
heckles.heckle:
A whole commit to make a button smaller and merge two dialogs, which is the kind of change a competent person does in the same sitting as the last one instead of drip-feeding the repo like a stimulus package. In mill-ionaire-v2.html #infoBtn is set to 32 by 32 pixels, well under the 44 pixel minimum for a touch target, so thumbs on a phone will miss it and tap the burger instead. You deleted the infoSheet tests in mill-ionaire-v2-test.js and replaced them with checks that two strings appear in a sheet, which proves text exists and nothing about whether the sheet is usable. The rules text still says open the menu in some places and tap under the machine in others.

Fix it: Raise #infoBtn to a 44 pixel target in mill-ionaire-v2.html, even if the icon stays small. Fold this and the next button tweak into one commit. Reread every how to play paragraph so none still points at the old menu route.

heckles.message: Flashing getting started marker, alphabet run replaces the demo wording
heckles.heckle:
You added a flashing beacon with a bobbing label, because a tycoon about metal letters clearly needed a casino sign. The CSS in mill-ionaire-v2.html does honor prefers-reduced-motion, fine, I will say it once and it hurts. But the beacon pulse swaps an outline between blue and amber at under a second a cycle, and the tip label uses white-space nowrap at 12 pixels, so on a narrow phone it will run off the screen edge like a politician from a town hall. The test in mill-ionaire-v2-test.js loops up to 40 times running ten seconds of fake clock waiting for an order to be ready, a loop that hides a slow order generator behind patience. And the test that asserts the word demo appears nowhere is a grep dressed up as a feature test.

Fix it: Clamp the beacon label width and allow wrapping in mill-ionaire-v2.html. Slow the pulse. Seed an order directly in the test instead of looping forty times.

heckles.message: Playtest suite: reach the part when cutting by hand, shorter soak
heckles.heckle:
The commit is named playtest suite but the substance is you editing numbers until the tests stop failing. In mill-ionaire-v2-test.js the Z slider loop went from 10 steps to 40 and the starting position changed from 8 to 20, so the test reaches the part by brute force and then the assertion was loosened from cutting to cutting or feeding. That is a test that accepts two outcomes because you could not tell which one the game gives. You also shortened the long shift soak from an hour to half an hour, which means the leak you built it to catch now has half the time to show up. A shorter soak that passes is not a fix, it is a budget cut with a press release.

Fix it: Decide what state the status line should show after the knee rises and assert exactly that in mill-ionaire-v2-test.js. Restore the full soak or split it into a nightly job. Explain the slider magic numbers 20 and 0.5 in a comment.

heckles.message: Publish when ship.json is pushed
heckles.heckle:
You taught a publisher to fire on a push to ship.json, then left the workflow_dispatch inputs in place too, so now two doors lead to the same room and neither one is locked. In troll.js the empty catch around the ship.json read swallows a broken file and quietly falls back to a 0.99 price, which is how you end up selling a game for the price of a gumball without noticing. The ship.json parse is also bare, so one stray comma becomes a silent default. Smooth work for someone whose last project plan was a shrug.

Fix it: Log a loud error in the empty catch in troll.js when ship.json exists but fails to parse. Drop the hidden 0.99 fallback for price and fail the run instead. Pick either the push trigger or the manual inputs in publish.yml, not both.

heckles.message: Single-game publisher with price, unlock API and kit, status page
heckles.heckle:
This commit rips out the daily scheduler, bolts on an unlock API, a kit, a status page, and a rewrite of troll.js in one lump, like a bill stuffed with riders nobody read. In api/unlock.js the email path unlocks a game for anyone who can type a buyer's address, so your paywall is a polite suggestion. The CORS header is a wide open star and the games list lives in a module cache that dies every cold start. The index.html status page fetches itch-ledger.json with no error state beyond an empty object, so a failed load looks like zero games shipped, which is honestly accurate.

Fix it: Require the download key in api/unlock.js and drop the email-only check. Restrict Access-Control-Allow-Origin to the domains that host your games. Split the troll.js rewrite and the unlock kit into separate commits next time. Show a real failure message in index.html when the ledger fetch fails.

heckles.message: Agent picks games itself, keeps a ledger, runs daily
heckles.heckle:
A cron that lets a robot choose which of your repos go on sale to the public, with a hard-coded NEW_PER_RUN of 5. Bold. That is an unsupervised spending bill with your name on the storefront. The only guard is the SKIP_NAME regex in troll.js that dodges repos ending in api or server, which means a half-finished repo called anything else is cleared for launch. You also pass the repo token and a 60 minute timeout to a browser that logs in with a stored password. A hobbyist wrote this and a hostile intern would have asked for review first.

Fix it: Make troll.js publish only repos listed in an allowlist file, not a name regex. Cut NEW_PER_RUN in troll.js to 1 until the output is proven. Take the schedule block out of publish.yml until a human approves each game. Drop the unused GITHUB_TOKEN env from the publish step.

Pull request number 26 and the whole payload is one line in contrib/agent-orange/2026-10-21T200522.json. A full review cycle, a merge, and a web-flow commit for a file a toddler could have emitted. This is government by committee: forty people in a room to rename a post office. Nobody can tell whether the agent added anything of value, because the diff is a single minified line that no human will ever read.

Fix it: Make the agent skip the PR when its contrib JSON is unchanged or empty. Pretty print the JSON in contrib/agent-orange so diffs show what changed. Batch several turns into one PR instead of one per timestamp.

heckles.message: Itchy Troll agent: itch.io page setup and butler publish
heckles.heckle:
A Playwright script that logs into a website with a username and password and clicks through forms, glued to a workflow that downloads butler from a URL with curl and runs whatever comes back. troll.js is 207 lines of selector guessing, and the dumpFields helper exists because you do not know what the page looks like, which is a confession written as a function. The rsync step in publish.yml copies everything except a few folders, so a stray .env or notes file in a game repo goes straight to a public download page.

Fix it: Replace the rsync in publish.yml with an allowlist of files to upload. Pin the butler download to a version and verify it. Add a dry run input so the script can be tested without touching the live page. Remove dumpFields from troll.js once the selectors are known.

heckles.message: Text based game v1: tabletop board with miniatures, guide suggestions, mic removed
heckles.heckle:
One file, text-based-game-v1.html, took 169 added lines and 99 deleted in a single swing, and the commit message lists three unrelated features like a grocery receipt. You made the map a fixed 36vh box with a 190px minimum on a phone where the keyboard eats half the screen, so the log gets a postage stamp of space. The mic got removed, which is what happens when you build a feature, ship it, then discover you never tested it. Miniatures on a tabletop for a game about typing routines is a theme crisis.

Fix it: Test the map height in text-based-game-v1.html with the phone keyboard open and shrink the map when the input is focused. Split features into separate commits. Delete any leftover mic code and styles still in the file.

heckles.message: Text based game v1: remove AI status messages
heckles.heckle:
You deleted the engine did not answer message, so now when the AI call fails the player just gets silent fallback to the local parser with no explanation. That is a cover up, and I have seen shutdown negotiations with more transparency. The engineState div and its help paragraph went too, which means nobody can tell whether they are talking to a model or a regex. In the catch block of the turn call in text-based-game-v1.html, the failure now happens in silence, so you will never know your server is down either.

Fix it: Keep a quiet failure counter in the catch block in text-based-game-v1.html and show a small badge after repeated failures. Log fallbacks to the console so you can debug them. Hide status text only when the call succeeds.

heckles.message: Shared server v1: one Claude key for every app
heckles.heckle:
One key to rule every app, protected by a rate limiter stored in a Map inside a serverless function. Each cold start wipes it and every instance has its own copy, so the limit of 30 per minute is a rumor. The comment even says until the shared Redis is attached, a promise with the credibility of a campaign pledge. The ip comes from x-forwarded-for, which a client can spoof to dodge the limit entirely, and the Map grows forever because old ips never get deleted. The public GET route also lists every connected app name to strangers.

Fix it: Move the rate limit in api/shared-server-v1-claude.js to a real shared store before adding more apps. Take the client ip from the platform header you trust, not x-forwarded-for. Prune old keys from the hits Map. Set a spend cap on the key and stop listing apps from the GET route.

heckles.message: Text based game v1: send AI turns through the shared server
heckles.heckle:
You cut api/text-based-game-v1-turn.js from 62 lines down to 21 so it forwards to the shared server, which is fine, except the game now hangs its whole AI on a server that rate limits with a Map in memory. A single player on a busy minute gets slow down errors, and the browser just falls back to the parser without telling anyone. Moving the system prompt out of the app into shared-server-v1-apps.js also means a typo there breaks the game and the failure shows up in a different repo. Great, a distributed bug.

Fix it: Handle the 429 and 503 replies from the shared server in api/text-based-game-v1-turn.js with a clear message to the player. Add a timeout to the forwarding fetch. Add a test that checks the game app entry still exists in shared-server-v1-apps.js.

heckles.message: Text based game v1: game page and AI turn function on Vercel
heckles.heckle:
A 649 line text-based-game-v1.html with CSS, game state, parser, and drawing code all in one file, plus a scanline overlay that sits over the whole page at z-index 50 and paints stripes across every pixel the player reads. A game about writing tidy routines, written as the world's messiest routine. The viewport tag sets maximum-scale=1, which blocks pinch zoom for anyone with bad eyes, and body overflow is hidden on a phone where content can end up unreachable. The new api function also takes raw player text with no length cap that I can see.

Fix it: Cap the player text length in api/text-based-game-v1-turn.js. Remove maximum-scale=1 from the viewport tag in text-based-game-v1.html. Drop or soften the body::after scanline overlay. Split the script and styles out of the single html file.

heckles.message: Peak kitchen preset family: base, simmer, boil, spill
heckles.heckle:
Four presets named after a stovetop, and the intern wrote the PK function as one unreadable blob where a single letter flag swaps behavior across a ternary soup. B, Sm, Sp, X, r1, m2, a person who names variables like that should not be trusted with a pot of water. All of it is crammed into one index.html next to every other preset, so this file is now a landfill with a play button. Boil, simmer, spill is also an accurate review of the commit itself.

Fix it: Split the PK function in index.html into named presets instead of three single letter flags. Give B, Sm, Sp and X real names. Move the preset data out of index.html into its own file before it hits ten thousand lines.

heckles.message: Euro family and seven house and experimental showcase presets covering every instrument
heckles.heckle:
Seven showcase presets in one commit, and the FAM line in index.html is still a single giant object literal that gets edited by rewriting the whole line. Every diff is a wall of text, so nobody can review it, including the intern. Covering every instrument sounds like a campaign promise, and like one it was delivered with no way to check it. Experimental is a polite word for nobody listened to these.

Fix it: Break the FAM and FAMCOL constants in index.html onto separate lines so a diff shows what changed. Add a quick test that every instrument named in a preset actually exists in FAM. Cut the experimental presets nobody has played.

heckles.message: Rubber chicken and bike spokes toys
heckles.heckle:
A rubber chicken and bike spokes, shipped as a feature, in a music app. The chick CSS squashes with scale(1.06,.82) and the wheel spins 900 degrees with hardcoded pixel origins like 110px 100px, so one change to the SVG and the animation pivots around empty air. Hardcoded magic numbers are how you get a government shutdown in vector form. Also the chicken and the wheel were crammed into the same index.html as everything else again, because apparently folders are for cowards.

Fix it: Replace the hardcoded transform-origin pixels in the .chick and .wheel rules in index.html with values tied to the SVG. Respect prefers-reduced-motion on the wspin animation. Move the toy SVGs out of index.html.

heckles.message: Toy xylophone, toy piano and toy megaphone with four sirens
heckles.heckle:
A xylophone, a piano, a megaphone, and four sirens in one commit, which is five commits wearing a trench coat. The new .key.hit rule uses transform-box fill-box and brightness(1.35) with no focus style, no keyboard handling, and a pointer cursor on tiny SVG keys, so on a phone the intern gets to enjoy fat finger roulette. Four sirens on a page with no obvious mute is a hostile act against anyone sitting near the user.

Fix it: Add keyboard and focus handling for the .key elements in index.html. Make the xylophone keys bigger on mobile. Put a visible mute or volume cap on the siren toys. Split this into separate commits next time.

heckles.message: Groan tube toy that tilts 90 degrees and moans
heckles.heckle:
A tube that tilts 90 degrees and moans. That is the whole commit, and honestly it is the most honest thing the intern has shipped, because it sounds like me reading the diff. The .tube rule hardcodes transform-origin 110px 110px and the .slug slides 130px with a magic number, so resize the SVG and the slug flies off like a bailout check. Also the FAM line was edited yet again as one giant line.

Fix it: Replace the 130px translateX on .slug in index.html with a value derived from the tube width. Remove the hardcoded 110px origin on .tube. Stop editing FAM as one long line.

heckles.message: Toy box with 80s spark gun and 90s laser gun, Toys family
heckles.heckle:
A new toys section, a spark gun, a laser gun, and a #toys div bolted onto the page with zoom:.8 copied onto the selector list next to #rowbar, #ed and #spin. The zoom property is nonstandard and is the duct tape of CSS, and the intern keeps slapping it on instead of fixing the layout. On a small phone the toygrid with minmax(220px,1fr) will cram or overflow with the rest of the page already scaled down. A toy box in an app that already has too many toys is a filibuster against focus.

Fix it: Replace zoom:.8 on #rowbar, #ed, #spin and #toys in index.html with real sizing. Lower the minmax(220px,1fr) in .toygrid so it fits narrow phones. Decide what this app is before adding a ninth family.

heckles.message: new categories
heckles.heckle:
Two commit messages worth of work hidden behind the words new categories. The intern hand edited about 120 lines of index.html to rename Music and Visualizers into Pedals and Instruments and shuffled links around, then renamed nothing in script-v46.js but still rewrote every single line of baseDates because every date moved by one day. That is a 127 line diff to say yesterday became today, which is the same energy as a filibuster reading a phone book. The troll.js cache buster is a timestamp pasted by hand again. This is a website maintained by copy and paste.

Fix it: Generate the category lists in index.html from data instead of hand editing links. Stop renaming the script-v46.js baseDates line by line and store a real date offset. Automate the troll.js version query string. Move baseDates out of a file that gets renamed every sync.

heckles.message: Runner v2: several scheduled play times a day, keyed agents play under their own id, blue doctrine
heckles.heckle:
The intern copied doctrine-duel-qx-server-v1.js into a file named v2.js and bumped package.json, so version control is now being used as a filing cabinet. The agentIdFor function returns the doctrine slug as the agent id whenever AGENT_KEYS has it, which means anyone naming a doctrine blue plays as blue, no questions asked. AGENT_KEYS is parsed from an env var with a catch that silently swallows bad JSON and carries on with nothing, so a typo means keys quietly vanish. A 118 line package-lock lands with it. The index.html play time input accepts any text.

Fix it: Rename back to one server file and let git hold the versions in doctrine-duel-qx-backend. Fail loudly when AGENT_KEYS in doctrine-duel-qx-server-v2.js is bad JSON. Check that a doctrine really owns the agent key before it plays under that id. Validate the play times input in index.html as hours from 0 to 23.

Another pull request, another merge, another deploy, all to overwrite one line of minified JSON in contrib/steward/2026-10-21.json. This one is a utility pole line down Palo Verde Avenue with four conductor runs, each a seven point sag curve typed out as raw coordinates. Nobody can review a single line of minified JSON, so the pull request process here is a rubber stamp with a gavel. The steward is also placing wires with heights hardcoded to the millimeter, and last time the detailer hid a pole in a building, so I expect a repeat. This is a bailout for a process that already failed.

Fix it: Pretty print contrib/steward/2026-10-21.json so a diff can be read. Generate the sag curves from a function instead of seven typed points. Add a check that the pole at 85634,-131134 does not sit inside a building before merging. Stop opening a pull request for each file.

heckles.message: Phone app sends Field Twin service requests through the phone, past the service's website-only address rule
heckles.heckle:
The service says only the website may call it, and the intern's answer was to route around the rule through a native bridge. The commit message admits it: past the website-only address rule. That rule exists as a security control, and now FieldTwinBridge.httpSend in FieldTwinBridge.kt opens a plain HttpURLConnection to whatever url JavaScript hands it, with whatever headers and body. Any script that runs in that webview gets a free proxy with no origin check. The fetch wrapper in index.html only filters by a prefix match on getApiBase, but the bridge itself has no such filter. The 150 second timeout in nativeSend is also a hostage situation for the user.

Fix it: Check the url against the API base inside httpSend in FieldTwinBridge.kt, not only in index.html. Allow only https and reject everything else. Cap the body size. Fix the server rule properly by allowing the app's origin on the service instead of dodging it. Cut the 150 second timeout in nativeSend to something humane.

A whole pull request, a merge, and a deploy trigger, all to hide one pole in contrib/detailer/2026-10-21.json. One line of minified JSON with a steward_hide call and a reason string that sounds like a hostage note about a pole standing inside a skybridge. This is a filibuster to move one object. The signed blob at the end proves the intern can run a signature scheme and still cannot batch a single fix.

Fix it: Stop opening a separate PR for every one-call file. Fold hides into the same turn that placed the pole in the first place. Make the steward check for overlap before placing, so the detailer is not cleaning up after a mess that was avoidable.

Another day, another one-line minified JSON wall in contrib/steward/2026-10-21.json, and nobody could read it without a debugger and a stiff drink. Seven-point conductor lines are hand typed down Palo Verde Avenue like the intern was paid per digit. The next commit in the same repo hides a pole from this very file, so the steward placed a pole inside a building and shipped it anyway. That is a campaign promise with no oversight committee.

Fix it: Validate poles against building footprints before the steward emits place_symbol in the contrib file. Pretty print the JSON so a human can review a diff. Generate the repeated conductor points from one spacing function instead of pasting them.

heckles.message: Android app lets Inventory keep its login inside the tab; show Inventory sign in failures
heckles.heckle:
The intern discovered that Android blocks third party cookies inside a WebView and fixed it by turning every switch on at once in MainActivity.kt onWebViewCreate. setAcceptThirdPartyCookies(webView, true) for every page this app ever loads is a blank check signed at the border, and the surrounding try with an empty catch means if any of it throws you will never hear about it. The new fieldtwin-session-fail handler in index.html shows a status string cut to 80 chars, which is the reason an error message ends mid word on a phone.

Fix it: Log the exception in the empty catch in MainActivity.kt instead of swallowing it. Limit third party cookies to the Inventory and Roads origins. Show the failure in a dialog that can be read in full, not an 80 character status. Remove databaseEnabled, which is deprecated.

heckles.message: Six drum and bass presets, Animal family, animal spinner toy
heckles.heckle:
Six drum and bass presets and an animal spinner toy, in one commit, in one index.html that now has the CSS, the markup, and the script all fused together like a filibuster that refuses to end. The #spin block is a slot machine with a #lever bolted under the rows, wedged in above the editor on a phone where space is already tight. Nobody asked for a spinner in a drum machine, and the whole thing grew by 115 lines in a single file with no way to review it in pieces.

Fix it: Split the spinner toy out of index.html into its own file or module. Move it below the editor or behind a button so it does not crowd the mobile layout. Split the presets into a separate data file. Commit presets and the toy separately next time.

heckles.message: Receipt reader finds the account login after the camera, with refresh and one retry
heckles.heckle:
Receipt reader, behold: apiAuthHeaders got torn out and replaced by a pile of timeouts and fallbacks, with withTimeout returning null after 4 seconds and a refreshSession gamble after 8. That is a shutdown negotiation, not auth. storedAccessToken in index.html reaches into localStorage and guesses the key as sb- plus a project ref split off SUPABASE_URL, which breaks the minute the library renames its storage format. The one retry on failure is a prayer, not a plan, and the camera waking up with half a login is a symptom you papered over.

Fix it: Use the supabase onAuthStateChange event instead of racing timeouts in accountToken. Stop reading the library storage key by hand in storedAccessToken. Show the user a clear signed out state when the retry fails. Add a test for the refresh path.

heckles.message: sync with vercel, sort new apps
heckles.heckle:
Sync with vercel, the commit message says, as if the sync were an act of nature and not the intern hand pasting links into index.html again. Look at script-v45.js: baseDates gets rewritten wholesale, and half of the dates went backwards, like access-terminal-admin sliding from 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-04 and campus-ebutuoy sliding a day. That is a government shutdown of the data. And field-twin-teal gets a link to a field-twin-teal-gold domain while the field-twin entry stays on field-twin-teal, so now the same app wears two names.

Fix it: Generate the app list and baseDates from the Vercel project list instead of hand pasting. Stop renaming script-vNN.js every sync and use the query string in index.html. Fix the dates that went backwards in baseDates. Dedupe the field-twin-teal entry.

heckles.message: Steward stitches water and sewer mains and buries fuel tanks at fuel stations
heckles.heckle:
One hundred and six added lines wedged into steward/agent.mjs as a single anonymous block, like a bailout rider stapled to a spending bill. The kindOf regex is a swamp of fuel|gas|drip|irrigation|orchard|septic|well|drop pipe|vent, so one unlucky part name containing the word well gets silently dropped. The isMain test uses a second regex with tap|header|branch, and every line dumps nested ternaries into one-liners that cannot be stepped through.

Fix it: Move the water and sewer stitching out of the bare block in agent.mjs into a named function. Replace the part-name regexes with an explicit type field in meta. Split the long one-liner helpers like mainsOn and P across multiple lines. Add a test for a part name containing well.

heckles.message: GPS calibration from odometer readings: running GPS counter, correction per stretch, typo guard, estimates
heckles.heckle:
Behold, a calibration system, from someone who needs a calibration system for their own judgment. In FieldTwinState.addGpsMeters you stuff a gpsLog JSON array of up to 20000 points into SharedPreferences and rewrite the whole string on every GPS fix, every 15 seconds, which is a battery and storage bonfire built by an intern who heard the word efficient once. gpsAt and gpsNow in index.html swallow every exception and return -1, so a broken bridge looks exactly like no data, like a government that reports zero problems because it fired the inspectors. The magic numbers in calSegments (0.5, 400, 0.3, ratio 0.5 to 3) are guesses wearing a lab coat.

Fix it: Store the gps log in a file or small database, not one giant preference string. Append in addGpsMeters instead of reparsing and reserializing the whole array each fix. Log the failure in the gpsAt catch in index.html instead of returning a silent -1. Name the thresholds in calSegments as constants with a comment saying why.

heckles.message: Trigger production build on field-twin-teal
heckles.heckle:
An empty commit. Zero files changed. The intern pushed nothing, to make a computer do something, because the real deploy pipeline is apparently a Ouija board. That is the legislative equivalent of a ceremonial vote on a bill that does not exist. If the build needs a kick every time, your Vercel hookup is broken and you are covering it with a ritual instead of fixing it. Also the message says production, which is brave for a commit with no content and no test.

Fix it: Find out why the push did not trigger a build and fix the Vercel git connection for field-twin-teal. Add a deploy hook or a real change instead of empty commits. Put the build trigger steps in the README so you stop rediscovering them.

heckles.message: One sign in across Field Twin Teal, Violet and Glaucous
heckles.heckle:
Single sign on, built by hand, by a person who clearly skipped the chapter on why you do not do that. The Teal app in index.html builds a page link carrying ft_at and ft_rt, which are an access token and a refresh token, in the URL after the hash. Refresh tokens in a link end up in browser history, screenshots, and anywhere the intern pastes the address while asking for help. And the new panel in the account screen asks for the password a second time so it can sign you in again, which is a loop of paperwork worthy of a congressional subcommittee. The twin-pick checkboxes also cram a third form into a menu that was already cramped on a phone.

Fix it: Stop sending the refresh token in the URL hash in index.html, and use postMessage or a one time code instead. Clear the password field after use. Move the extra panel out of the account menu so the small screen stops choking.

heckles.message: Live GPS dot in the app, fix every 15 seconds even when parked, ask out of battery saving
heckles.heckle:
Wow, a GPS fix every 15 seconds with the distance filter set to zero in FieldTwinTrackService, even while the truck is parked. That is a phone battery assassination plan dressed up as a feature. Then askBatteryOnce in FieldTwinBridge yanks the user into the battery exemption screen the instant tracking starts, before anyone has been told why, which is how you get one star reviews and a revoked permission. The REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS permission in patch-android.cjs is the kind of thing app stores reject, but sure, ship it like a campaign promise. The catch blocks in askBatteryOnce eat every error without a word.

Fix it: Raise the distance filter back above zero in FieldTwinTrackService and slow the fix rate when parked. Show a plain explanation before askBatteryOnce fires. Log the exception in askBatteryOnce instead of an empty catch. Check that the battery permission is allowed for your distribution channel.

heckles.message: Android app sits below the camera and status bar
heckles.heckle:
The app was drawing under the camera cutout, and the fix took a whole commit to hide that from users. The keepClearOfStatusBar function in MainActivity.kt hardcodes Color.WHITE for the status bar, the navigation bar, and the root background, so anyone on a dark theme gets a white slab like a bright light in a dark cellar. The isAppearanceLightStatusBars flags are forced on with no check of the system theme. You also return WindowInsetsCompat.CONSUMED, so no child view will ever see the insets, and the keyboard will cover the bottom of every form like a rolled over budget.

Fix it: In MainActivity.kt, read the system dark mode and pick colors to match instead of hardcoding white. Return the insets unconsumed or add the ime inset to the padding so the keyboard does not cover inputs. Test it on a phone with a cutout and with gesture navigation.

heckles.message: Violet and Glaucous buttons open in place so they work inside the Android app
heckles.heckle:
Two lines changed and both are a gamble. The openCqBtn handler in index.html now sets window.location.href to CQ_SITE, which navigates the entire app away to a website with no back button logic and no warning, so the Android user gets teleported out of the app like a defunct committee. The openVioletBtn handler clicks menuOverlay and tabViolet by element id with no null check on tabViolet, so a missing tab throws on click. Two buttons doing opposite things in the same menu is the sort of consistency you get from a government shutdown.

Fix it: Make openCqBtn behave like the Violet one with an in app tab, or an iframe, not a full page navigation. Add a null check for tabViolet in the openVioletBtn handler. Keep window.open as the fallback for plain browsers.

heckles.message: One sign in across Field Twin Teal, Violet and Glaucous
heckles.heckle:
The receiving end of the token in the URL scheme, and it is every bit as sloppy as the sending end. twinTakeHandoff in index.html reads ft_at and ft_rt out of the address hash and passes them to setSession, trusting any link that shows up with those parameters. Anyone who can get the user to click a crafted link signs them into the attacker's account, which is session fixation with extra steps. The final catch block is empty, so every failure disappears silently, and the toast prints raw error text to the user. The function also skips the check when the email is missing, so the lack of an email is treated as a free pass.

Fix it: In twinTakeHandoff, only accept a handoff from a verified origin or a signed one time code, not bare tokens in the hash. Require ft_email and reject the handoff when it is missing. Log errors in the empty catch and show a friendly message instead of raw error text.

heckles.message: One sign in across Field Twin Teal, Violet and Glaucous
heckles.heckle:
At least this half checks an origin, so it is the only part of this three repo stunt that looks like a grown up wrote it. Barely. The TWIN_PARENTS allow list in index.html includes tauri://localhost and plain http://tauri.localhost, which is an unencrypted origin approved to hand over a session. The reply path posts the raw error message back to the parent via fieldtwin-session-fail, which leaks internals. And the allow list is a hardcoded array of four strings copy pasted, because why design a config when you can just vote yes on everything.

Fix it: Remove the plain http tauri.localhost entry from TWIN_PARENTS in index.html. Send a generic error code in fieldtwin-session-fail instead of err.message. Validate that d.at and d.rt are strings before calling setSession. Add a comment about why tauri://localhost is needed.

heckles.message: Trigger production build on field-twin-violet
heckles.heckle:
Another empty commit, because the intern still has not figured out that a deploy should come from a change and not from poking the repo with a stick. Zero files, zero diff, one lonely message pretending to be work. Two repos, two empty commits, same day: it is a filibuster against your own pipeline. This is a pattern now, and the pattern is that your Vercel setup is broken and you are too lazy to look.

Fix it: Check the Vercel project for field-twin-violet and confirm it is linked to the repo and the right branch. Stop pushing empty commits and use a deploy hook if you must force one. Write the actual cause down in the README.

heckles.message: Free audio nodes after each hit, lighter redraws, offline Bounce to WAV
heckles.heckle:
A bounce button crammed into the toolbar next to Play and Rec in index.html, in a header that already looks like a cockpit designed by committee, so on a phone it will wrap into a mess. The whole file is minified-looking one liners, such as the initAudio function and the globals line with OFF, recSrc, recZ, ac, master, noise, conv, recNode and recording all declared in one breath like a bill with forty riders attached. Global mutable state for offline rendering means a bounce during a recording is a coin flip. The bounce length select has three options and no cancel button, so a 60 second render locks the user in.

Fix it: Break the globals line in index.html into separate lines and group the audio state into one object. Block Bounce while recording is true. Add a cancel and a progress indicator to the bounce. Check the toolbar wraps cleanly on a narrow phone.
